For an AGGREGATE, flatten the repetitions with the `*` wildcard: Sum(Lines*/Amount), NumberOfFilledFields(Lines*/Sku), NumberOfFilledGroups(Lines*). For a PER-REPETITION predicate (RepetitionNotUnique / CurrentRepetition), make the rule iterate by putting its group at the PARENT of the repeated group with the error field inside it — via the CLI, `rule check --group <parentGroup> --field <parentGroup>/<repeatedGroup>/<field>` (e.g. --group /Order --field /Order/Items/Sku for RepetitionNotUnique(Items/Sku)).
diagnostics.explain: MVK_NO_WILDCARD fires when a repeatable group is referenced from a non-iterating scope: the kernel expected either a flattening `*` (aggregates) or a rule that iterates over that group (per-repetition predicates). The required form depends on the operator, so this code is not specific to any single one.

diagnostics.summary: Rule with path '/It/CheckRule': Corrupt input or condition not complete (yet): Unexpected found '['. [MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN]
diagnostics.fix: The condition has a token the DSL parser did not expect (a syntax slip the kernel reports with no message of its own). The most common causes, in order: (1) a BOOLEAN literal must be CAPITALIZED — write `True` / `False`, not the JSON `true` / `false` (e.g. `[Flag] == True`); (2) a string value must be DOUBLE-QUOTED — `[Status] == "OPEN"`; (3) operator/keyword names are case-sensitive PascalCase — `FieldFilled`, `And`, `Or`, `Not`; (4) a FIELD used as a comparison VALUE must be BRACKETED — `[Approved] != True`, not `Approved != True` (bare names belong only inside a function/predicate's parentheses, like `FieldFilled(Approved)`). Re-check the token at the reported position against these.
diagnostics.explain: MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN is the kernel's generic parse error — a token appeared where the grammar did not allow it — and it is raised WITHOUT a message, so the likely cause has to be inferred from the DSL's literal/keyword conventions (capitalized booleans True/False, double-quoted strings, case-sensitive PascalCase operators).

diagnostics.summary: Rule with path '/It/CheckRule': The error field '/It/A' is not referenced in the condition. [MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED]
diagnostics.fix: Name the rule's error field somewhere in the condition. Most often this is a model-level aggregate rule whose condition only references the aggregated per-row path — reference the error field by comparing the aggregate AGAINST it (`[FeeCap] < Sum(Lines*/Amount)` references FeeCap) or by guarding with `FieldFilled(<the error field>) And …`.
diagnostics.explain: Every rule's error field must appear among the fields its condition references — the kernel attaches the fired error to that field and rejects a condition that never names it. An aggregate's starred path does not reference the (non-repeatable) error field, so model-level aggregate rules hit this unless the error field is referenced explicitly.
